title: Study questions: Personal injury and public information
shortTitle: Study questions: Personal injury and public information
summary: The assigned notes ask how courts should distinguish shared constitutional grievances from statutory informational injuries.
notes:
The casebook asks why a Black housing tester’s statutory right to truthful information supports a claim while a citizen’s interest in CIA-budget information under a constitutional provision did not support Richardson’s suit. It also compares contractors’ equal opportunity to compete with a taxpayer’s interest in an informed electoral process. Analyze the interest asserted, the relevant text, the claimant’s relation to it, and whether Congress expressly authorized review.

A second question follows Sunstein’s discussion: if Congress can create an enforceable informational interest, how far can it recognize interests in preservation of distant landscapes or endangered species? State Sunstein’s argument and then test it against the assigned TransUnion and Spokeo limits. The notes frame this as a disputed question; no single model answer is represented as the professor’s view.
